summary: This Xbox 360 recompilation proves how good fan ports can be when they aren't vibe-coded.
body: When Final Fantasy creator Hironobu Sakaguchi left Square Enix in the early 2000s, he started a new studio, Mistwalker, to keep making RPGs. For the last 20 years, every single one of his games with the exception of Fantasian has been stuck on one defunct console or another, never ported or re-released. And that's a shame, because some of them are great RPGs. (Image credit: Mistwalker) Or I should say it was a shame, until now—because as of Friday, Blue Dragon will be playable on PC thanks to a fan-made port that's likely far more impressive than an official release ever would've been. re:Blue, a static recompilation of the Dragon Quest-inspired JRPG, follows in the footsteps of the unofficial Sonic Unleashed PC port that proved how effective fan-made ports can be. These projects cleverly translate the original game code to run natively on modern PCs, but don't include any of the original assets to avoid copyright issues. body: Hello from Gamescom 2026 , where yours truly has been trying out some of the latest laptops at the Nvidia booth. The machines I was shown are made by various manufacturers, but all of them have the same core internal hardware, in the form of Nvidia's RTX Spark SOC. Which means that, alongside 20 Grace CPU cores in the custom Arm-based chip, they've also got 6144 RTX Blackwell GPU cores to play with. And that means RTX 5070 -like gaming performance, at least on paper. And in practice, each was demonstrated to be capable of running modern games at high frame rates. Exactly how high was kept under wraps, unfortunately, although it was mentioned that frame generation was in use for each. summary: فوز صعب للفريق السعودي
body: فوز صعب للفريق السعودي قاد صالح أبو الشامات، الأهلي السعودي، إلى الدور الثاني من كأس القارات للأندية 2026، بعد فوزه الصعب على ضيفه أوكلاند سيتي النيوزيلندي، بهدف نظيف، في اللقاء الذي جمعهما على ملعب الإنماء، ضمن الدور الأول للبطولة العالمية. وسجل صالح أبو الشامات، الهدف الوحيد في الدقيقة 63، بعد انطلاقة صاروخية إدوارد سبيرتسيان، من الجبهة اليمنى، الذي وصل إلى حدود منطقة الجزاء، ومرر كرة مميزة، لأبو الشامات، الذي لعبها ببراعة داخل الشباك، في أول لمسة له في المباراة. وضرب الأهلي موعدا مع صن داونز الجنوب أفريقي، يوم 19 سبتمبر، في الدور الثاني، على كأس القارات الثلاث: آسيا وأفريقيا وأوقيانوسيا. وجاءت المباراة خالية من الفرص الحقيقة باستثناء بعض المحاولات الأهلاوية، حيث أحكم أوكلاند دفاعه في الشوط الأول، الذي كان أقل من الشوط الثاني فيما يخص مستوى الفريقين. وفي الشوط الثاني تحسن أداء الأهلي، ونجح في تسجيل الهدف الوحيد، وأهدر عدة محاولات بعدها. من أول لمسة.. صالح أبو الشامات يسجل الهدف الأول للأهلي في شباك أوكلاند الأهلي 1 أوكلاند 0 #MBCACTION #الأهلي_أوكلاند pic.twitter.com/QfkgKSQUcI — MBC Action (@mbcaction) August 26, 2026

title: HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws'
summary: Everything about the studio's new game is different.
body: If you watched the Nodusfall trailer during Gamescom's Opening Night Live and, like me, thought the combo of Elden Ring's aesthetic and Monster Hunter's fights sounded awesome, but were worried about selling your soul to the god of gacha, fret not! Nodusfall isn't just a visual departure for HoYoverse, swapping the vibrant anime aesthetic for something gloomier, it also represents a (partial) change in business model. According to the devs, "Nodusfall will be a free-to-play, long-term game. What we can share at this time is that characters are not obtained through random draws. We hope to allow players to unlock this core gameplay experience through continued play. Cosmetic monetization is an important avenue we will be considering." In my hands-on, the four available characters could be customised with different outfits, hairstyles and accessories, and I can imagine folk dropping some cash on some new fits for their boss-slaying crew, but it's a relief to know that I won't need to go through RNG hell or wipe out my bank account just to play as a surly warrior who can transform into a dual-wielding giant. title: Micron, the trillion-dollar memory company, refused to replace a crucial drive for current market value until Reddit got mad
summary: 'Pushing back actually worked.'
body: With the memory crisis only continuing to get worse, a PC gamer's fear right now is likely their memory, storage or GPU borking, and needing to spend an inflated price to replace it. One such Redditor had an external drive die in just one year, and Crucial only offered a refund of the original price they paid, which was a lot less than similar drives go for now. That was until they brought their problems to Reddit. Over on the PCMR subreddit , user CarefulMeasurement99 shared that they bought a 4 TB Crucial drive a year ago for $200, and when it broke, Crucial offered that original price in a refund. That same drive seems to fetch up to $800 now (thanks, AI). Crucial originally set up an RMA for the drive in order to pick it up and send it back to the company. The Redditor replied to this saying, "Due to the recent global increase in SSD prices, $199.999 is unfortunately no longer enough to purchase a new 4 TB drive in the current market", and officially requested a direct replacement. This story gets a tad complicated because Micron announced the closure of the Crucial consumer business late last year, which threw its ability to actually replace the drive into question. title: MSI Stealth 16 AI+ B3W review
summary: Hella nice, but hella expensive. Thanks, 2026.
body: If there were ever a laptop design to be right "up my alley", as we brits like to say, it would be this one. That's because it makes its sacrifices in exactly the right places to deliver something genuinely portable, sleek, elegant, and satisfying to use both for gaming and work. The MSI 'Stealth' laptop looks to have been reimagined along these MacBook or Razer Blade-esque lines—and successfully so—featuring a giant touchpad, thin aluminium form factor, subtle upward-facing speakers, and a spacious screen. It's not just a looker, though, as MSI has crammed an RTX 5080 mobile GPU into it, making for genuine high-end performance. It has, however, had to be power-limited to play nicely with the slim chassis, meaning you're not getting quite the performance you could get out of a chunkier laptop for the same very expensive price or cheaper. Buy if... ✅ You use your laptop in public: This thing definitely looks the part alongside MacBooks and other such suave devices, with its aluminium frame and giant trackpad. ✅ You use a USB headset: I didn't have any of the audio latency issues I noticed when using USB earphones/headset. title: رئيس رابطة الدوريات الأوروبية: لا مكان لإنفانتينو في مستقبل الفيفا

title: Atari is taking another shot at reviving RollerCoaster Tycoon
summary: RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks is being developed by Springloaded, makers of the excellent Let's Build a Zoo.
body: Last we saw RollerCoaster Tycoon it was in pretty rickety shape. More than a decade after RollerCoaster Tycoon 3, the follow-up—RollerCoaster Tycoon World—was released to nearly universally poor reviews. Even worse, in one of the all-time dick moves in gaming industry history, Atari launched it exactly one day before rival sim Planet Coaster was due to release. Wow. That nakedly desperate move didn't help the situation: people liked Planet Coaster and didn't like RCTW, and the Tycoon series has been silent since 2016. But here we are another decade later, and Atari is bringing RollerCoaster Tycoon back yet again—though I'm already feeling more hopeful about it. RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks was announced at Gamescom today, and the new entry in the series is being developed by Springloaded, who made the excellent Let's Build a Zoo and is releasing promising gamedev sim Let's Build a Dungeon later this year. That's a good sign, at least! There's no date on the books yet, and RollerCoaster Tycoon Wonderworks won't be feature complete when it launches: it's "coming soon" to early access. title: DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction is a definite improvement but path traced fidelity is still not a 100% solved issue
summary: Nvidia has rounded out the DLSS 4.5 stack… now where's DLSS 5?
body: Nvidia's new DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction feature is laser-focused on trying to fix the second most annoying thing about ray traced or path traced games: visual artifacting. Yes, the lighting effect does deliver the most accurate-looking lighting and shadows in games, but in motion there is a definite visual weirdness added into scenes. And that weirdness generally comes from the denoising pass designed to turn the low-fidelity path traced image, with its limited number of rays, into a fully realised frame. Leave a game's viewport still and the scene will pretty rapidly come together to make a sharp, convincing image. Shift that around, or have that scene filled with moving objects or characters and you're going to see the sort of visual trails you might only have been used to in the warehouse parties of your early twenties. Just me? The issue is that it's way too expensive in terms of raw compute to trace every single photon/pixel that would otherwise make up a fully traced scene. Even with the current method of tracking a far smaller representative sample of rays bouncing around the geometry of your game world it's still incredibly demanding of your PC's hardware.
